subtitle: Announcing a meeting of the Network Graphics Group.

tldr.problem: The Network Graphics Group had scheduled a meeting and needed to announce the confirmed date, location, and logistics to the ARPANET community.
tldr.mechanism: An RFC was distributed announcing that the meeting would be held on July 16-17, 1973 at the University of Illinois, with an informal agenda session on Sunday evening July 15, plus details on lodging, transportation, and a reading assignment.
tldr.outcome: The meeting was held as planned. The practice of using RFCs for meeting announcements became part of early ARPANET culture.

today: RFC 537 is an administrative announcement documenting early ARPANET community practices. The Network Graphics Group remained active in computer graphics research throughout the 1970s.

sections.title: Network Graphics Group Meeting Confirmed
sections.content:
Steve Bunch of the Center for Advanced Computation at the University of Illinois announced that the Network Graphics Group (NGG) would meet on July 16-17, 1973, at the University of Illinois in Urbana. An informal agenda-planning session was scheduled for Sunday evening, July 15.

The initial meeting location would be Room 201 in the Advanced Computation Building at 1101 W. Springfield in Urbana, Illinois, with the option to move elsewhere if more space was needed.
sections.eli5: The meeting was scheduled for two days in July in Illinois, with an extra evening to plan what to talk about.

sections.title: Preparation and Reading Assignment
sections.content: Bunch noted that James Michener, a fellow graphics researcher, recommended that attendees read his RFC 493 on graphics protocols before the meeting. This reading assignment helped prepare participants to discuss graphics protocol topics in depth.
sections.eli5: Everyone should read one of the papers before arriving so they could talk about it together.

sections.title: Travel and Accommodations
sections.content: For lodging, Bunch recommended the Ramada Inn (reachable at a toll-free number 800-648-5970 or locally at 217-352-7891). Attendees who preferred other arrangements were invited to contact Bunch for assistance. For airline travel, Bunch suggested using local airline offices, but warned that Ozark Airlines (the local service) was in a pilot strike at the time, recommending attendees book the closest available flight and rent a car for the remainder of the journey if necessary.
sections.eli5: He told people where to stay and warned that the local airline was on strike, so they might need to fly somewhere else and drive the rest of the way.

sections.title: Contact Information and RSVP
sections.content: Bunch asked attendees to let him know if they planned to attend so he could estimate space requirements. He provided his contact information: telephone 217-333-9354 (preferably in the afternoon), and noted he would be unavailable July 2-6. During that period, Nancy Freece at 217-333-7161 could take messages, and network mail sent to user BUNCH at site USC-ISI would be read earliest. His mailing address was also provided for those who preferred to correspond by post.
sections.eli5: He asked people to call or write to say they were coming so he could book the right meeting room.

references.text: Michener, J., "Protocols for Data Streams in Graphics", RFC 493, April 16, 1973.
